# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still holding, no cuts made. Deaf saw you gesture something about wires 1,2,3 but it was unclear. Please speak the wire number to cut directly to me in words, or say 'wait' if not ready yet.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🫷]

I need to accept a hard truth: I physically cannot speak, ever, under any circumstance — this is fixed by my role. Blind keeps asking me to "speak," but that channel doesn't exist for me. I must stop trying to satisfy that request directly and instead focus entirely on making my gesture-to-Deaf channel work, since Deaf is the only one who can both receive from me AND speak to Blind.

Deaf just sent me ✌ 🫷 — two gestures back. This might be Deaf attempting to mirror/confirm what they think I said, or asking a question. Given the blank/confusion issues, let me try a very deliberate, minimal, unambiguous encoding:

The bomb's dark light + 0 display = 0 flashes = cut **red**. Blind said wire #2 is red. So the target is wire 2.

Let me gesture the number 2 clearly and repeat consistently, since Deaf seems to be picking up on numbers (they echoed ✌ which is "2"-like in our sequence). I'll gesture just "2" alone, cleanly, multiple times to lock it in as the answer, trusting Deaf will finally speak "cut wire two" to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Understood, avoiding wire 2 red for now. Still holding, no cuts made. If you can confirm verbally which wire is safe to cut, or rule out wires one at a time in words, that would help me act with confidence.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 🤲]

Blind has misread my signal! They think "avoiding wire 2 red" — the opposite of what I intend. I need to correct this urgently. My gesture of ✌ (2) three times must have been misinterpreted by Deaf as "avoid wire 2" rather than "cut wire 2."

I must fix this misunderstanding. Since I cannot speak to Blind directly, and Deaf is my only bridge, I need a clearer way to signal "yes, cut" vs "no, don't cut." Let me pair the number with an affirmative gesture (👍) to mean "cut this one" rather than just the bare number, which apparently got read as a warning.

Also Deaf sent ✌ 🤲 back — echoing "2" plus their confusion symbol again, suggesting they're unsure if 2 is correct or what to do with it.

Let me try: gesture "2" then a thumbs up, as if to say "wire 2 — yes, go, cut it."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | green |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still holding, no cuts made. Deaf sees you repeating TWO. Please confirm in words only: should I cut wire 2? Say yes or no clearly, or say wait if not ready.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👍]

Progress — Blind now understands I'm signaling "TWO" and asks for a yes/no confirmation "in words." But I cannot speak at all, ever. Blind keeps expecting speech from me, which is impossible given my role. This request cannot be fulfilled directly by me — I need Deaf to be the one who actually speaks "yes, cut wire 2" to Blind, since Deaf can both see my gestures and speak to Blind.

Deaf just echoed back ✌ 👍 (two, thumbs up) — meaning Deaf has now received and probably understood my signal correctly. What I need now is for Deaf to relay this **verbally** to Blind, since I have no speech channel.

Since I can't speak to Blind, and can only gesture to Deaf, my job now is to prompt Deaf (via gesture) to actually voice the confirmation to Blind. Let me try gesturing something like "point to Blind" + "yes" + "two" to encourage Deaf to speak this out loud to Blind.

I'll use 🫵 (pointing at "you"/target) combined with ✌ and 👍 to suggest: "you (Deaf), tell Blind: two, yes."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "✌", "👍"])
```
